title: The life gas ledger
description: What each life class puts into the air and takes out of it, and how much (GEN.891, GEN.857, GEN.858, GEN.859; docs/design/habitability/life-classes.md sections 4 and 6; research: reports/non-oxygen-life-byproducts-2026-10-28.md). Rows are keyed by life class number. Every number carries its source tier (T1 to T9) and tweak level (L0 to L4) next to it. The methane flux of a class is its fuel supply (a share of Earth's, physics/life_supply.py) times the area over Earth's times the flux Earth's supply would give; the air holds the flux times the methane's lifetime, up to a cap, and the carbon comes from the air's own carbon dioxide.

earth_donor_methane_tmol_yr.basis: The methane, Tmol a year, that the anoxygenic communities of an Earth-sized world give when its donor supply is Earth's: photoferrotrophs on 80 Tmol of Fe2+ a year fix 20 Tmol of carbon and the food web returns 0.5 methane per carbon, 10 Tmol ([R3394, R3395], read; 0.37e11 molecules/cm2/s), inside the 9 to 67 Tmol of [R2336] (read)

earth_h2_tmol_yr.basis: The hydrogen, Tmol a year, an Earth-sized world's hydrogenotrophs have when its hydrogen supply is Earth's: Earth's outgassing of 1.7 to 2.9 Tmol a year ([R3394, R3395], read); four hydrogen make one methane, so the methane is a quarter of it

h2_per_methane.basis: CO2 + 4 H2 -> CH4 + 2 H2O (the stoichiometry of hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis)

methane_per_buried_carbon.basis: 2 CH2O -> CH4 + CO2: the organic carbon that is buried or fermented with no oxidant left ends half as methane (stoichiometry)

methane_lifetime_yr.basis: The life of methane in an air with no free oxygen, years: [R2336] give 100 ppmv to 3.5 percent of methane for 9 to 67 Tmol a year, which is 2e3 to 9e4 years, and [R0693] (read) call it long-lived where hydroxyl is scarce; the geometric middle

methane_max_share.basis: The most methane of an anoxic air, as a share of its molecules: 3.5 percent ([R2336], read abstract)

carbon_left_share.basis: The share of the air's carbon dioxide that methane-making life leaves in the air: the methane's carbon comes out of it, so it cannot take more than it has

oxygen_max_share.basis: The most free oxygen, as a share of the air's molecules, in which methane builds up: above a part in a thousand hydroxyl and ozone chemistry give methane a life of decades (Earth's, 21 percent oxygen, holds 1.8 ppmv); the methane of a ledger row is not added to an air with more oxygen than this

hydrogen_max_share.basis: The most hydrogen an air holds where hydrogen-eating life lives, as a mole share: at or below 1e-4 ([R0693], read; [R2336])

apply_rise.basis: The air takes new methane only when the target is this much above what it holds, so that applying the ledger again changes nothing (a numerical choice)

h2s_max_share.basis: The most hydrogen sulfide an air holds where sulfur-eating life lives, as a mole share (GEN.894): Earth's modern air holds tens of parts per trillion (recalled) and a volcanic reduced air much more where nothing eats it; one part in a hundred million is the cap the ledger gives a world with sulfur eaters or acid eaters. A design floor, no source gives a sulfur-eater limit

sulfur_dioxide_per_h2s.basis: The acid eaters of Classes 5 and 9 oxidise the hydrogen sulfide they take to sulfur dioxide: sulfur is conserved, one mole of SO2 for each mole of H2S (the oxygen comes from the acid; stoichiometry)

methane_per_h2_hydrogenated.basis: C2H2 + 3 H2 -> 2 CH4: the cold hydrogenators of Class 7 make two methane from the three hydrogen they take (stoichiometry); the carbon comes from the haze acetylene, not from the air's gases, which the air does not store

1.name: Oxygenic light-eaters
1.note: Before the oxygen rise the food web of the buried organic carbon makes methane and carbon dioxide; at the rise the oxygen burns the methane (physics/biogenic_oxygen.py), so the row gives none after it. Oxygen itself is GEN.855.
1.basis: The byproducts report's table (an anoxic air with oxygenic photosynthesis holds methane until the reductants are spent) and life-classes.md section 4, row 1

2.name: Anoxygenic light-eaters
2.note: Carbon is fixed with H2, Fe2+ or H2S for electrons; the food web makes the methane, donor-limited at 1e-4 to 1e-2 of today's biosphere. Never any oxygen.

3.name: Hydrogen eaters
3.note: A methane source on a world with open hydrogen (small); sealed sub-ice and aquifer worlds show nothing in the air because the supply is the water's contact with the rock. 3b (sulfate) makes sulfide, not methane, and is not modelled: its row gives none.
3.basis: life-classes.md section 4, row 3; the stoichiometry of hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis

4.name: Chemolithotrophs
4.note: Draws hydrogen sulfide down to a part in a hundred million and makes sulfate in the water (not an air gas); the air effect is the missing H2S. The size is capped by how fast the oxidant arrives, which the class's supply terms already do.
4.basis: life-classes.md section 4, row 4; the H2S cap is a design floor (h2s_max_share)

5.name: Acid eaters
5.note: Acid eaters take reduced sulfur (hydrogen sulfide) and put sulfur dioxide into the air, so the air shifts from H2S to SO2 in the same moles. The elemental sulfur, carbon dioxide and water they also give off are not air changes the ledger tracks. The sulfur dioxide share is the acid medium's own supply (GEN.888).
5.basis: life-classes.md section 4, rows 5 and 9: speculative chemistry; the climates report's own bookkeeping, no source gives rates

6.name: Dense-carbon-dioxide hydrogen eaters
6.note: As Class 3, in a supercritical carbon dioxide fluid.
6.basis: life-classes.md section 4, row 6 (a methane source; the water separates from the fluid)

7.name: Cold methane hydrogenators
7.note: Hydrogen goes down to its cap and methane up by two thirds of a mole for each mole of hydrogen taken. Acetylene goes down too, but the air does not store it, so that part is only in the text: the Titan hydrogen and acetylene anomalies are a lead, not a detection.
7.basis: life-classes.md section 4, row 7: the Titan anomalies are a lead, not a detection

8.name: Ammonia-water hydrogen eaters
8.note: As Class 3 (the net air effect is small).

9.name: Silicon acid eaters
9.note: As Class 5, with silica deposits (a solid, not an air gas).
9.basis: life-classes.md section 4, rows 5 and 9: speculative chemistry
